newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Evangelical pastor arrested in Guatemala lynching.
newsitem.headline: Evangelical pastor arrested in Guatemala lynching.

text.p: An evangelical minister was arrested and charged with participating in a mob attack on two suspected baby-snatchers that left one woman dead, a police spokesman said on Wednesday.
Eugenio Nij, 39, pastor at the San Raymundo Church of God for 17 years, was arrested on Tuesday in connection with the March 5 lynching, Luis Lickas, spokesman for the National Police, said.
Zacarias Bac, 29, also was arrested, bringing to five the number of suspects held in jail, Lickas said.
Police estimated that about 1,000 people used stones, boards, bottles, and a home-made dumbbell to beat to death Maria del Carmen Gonzales, 23.
Elvira Caal, 24, also was injured in the attack in San Raymundo, about 13 miles (20 kms) northwest of the capital city.
Virtually "the entire population" of San Raymundo was involved, Lickas said, adding that the investigation could lead to additional arrests.

Villagers dragged the two women from the jail after police arrested them on suspicion of trying to snatch a child in the market. Investigators have since cast doubt, however, on whether they were attempting to steal anyone, Lickas said.
Mob lynching has become a gruesome trend in Guatemala, with at least nine men beaten and burned alive this year.
The San Raymundo case was unusual because its victims were women.
The attack echoed a March 1994 beating of a tourist, June Weinstock of Alaska, who was left severely disabled.

At that time a fear of foreigners taking babies to sell them or their body parts was sweeping Guatemala and Weinstock was attacked by a crowd of Guatemalans who believed she had tried to steal a baby.
